name: Meter SKU switch on BYOK completion (FR-BYOK-9 / AC-4)
skipReason: Effect is observable in the audit ledger payload (credential_source field) and the persisted ai_gateway.completion.billed_cost (0 for BYOK). Covered by integration test referenced in PRD AC-4.
description: Internal (non-HTTP) contract for completionService.emitCompletionEvent, which stamps credential_source ('tenant' or 'platform') into the ai-gateway.complete.v1 / ai-gateway.stream.v1 audit payload so the meter ingest worker knows which SKUs to emit (FR-BYOK-9 / AC-4). On a BYOK call the tenant pays the provider directly, so billed_cost is 0, the ai-gateway.tokens.* markup SKU is suppressed, and only the governance SKU is emitted; on a platform-credential call both SKUs are emitted and billed_cost carries the margin. QA edge cases: the entire emit is wrapped in try/catch and only console.errors on failure, so an audit-ledger outage NEVER fails or degrades the completion — the completion still returns 200 while the billing event is silently lost, which is the revenue-leak scenario to watch for; consequently this function has no error return path of its own; the effect is observable only in the audit ledger payload (credential_source) and the persisted ai_gateway.completion.billed_cost, not in any HTTP response body.

testCases.name: Tenant credential completion stamps credential_source=tenant and bills 0 markup
Platform credential completion stamps credential_source=platform and bills with margin

errorCases.message: [ai-gateway] audit emit failed for completion <completion_id> <reason> (console.error only)
errorCases.when: appendAuditEntry() throws inside emitCompletionEvent — audit pool AI_GATEWAY_AUDIT_POOL unreachable, the pool_index unknown, or the append rejected. The whole body is wrapped in try/catch (completionService.ts:301-333) and only console.errors, so the completion STILL returns 200 with its output while the billing event is lost. This is the revenue-leak case: no HTTP status ever reflects it, so QA must assert the audit.entry row exists rather than trusting the 2xx.

the event name is absent from EVENT_TYPE_REGISTRY in @projexlight/contracts (OC-2 rejects it before any write). Because the emit is swallowed, a renamed or unregistered type degrades to exactly the case above — a clean 200 with no ledger entry — rather than surfacing anywhere the caller can see.

complete() throws at completionService.ts:349-351 because the resolved provider row is missing or status='disabled'. completeHandler maps any message containing 'not available' or 'no route matches' to 503 (completionController.ts:42-45). Thrown BEFORE emitCompletionEvent is reached, so NO event is emitted at all and the meter sees neither SKU — distinct from the swallowed case, where the completion succeeded and only the event was lost.

ensureKillSwitchClear() -> assertKillSwitchDisengaged() throws KillSwitchError('[ai-gateway] kill-switch engaged for agent <agent_id> (flag <flag_id>)') at the top of complete() (FR-AGW-7 / G-9), before any provider cost is incurred. The message matches neither 503 substring, so completeHandler falls through to a generic 500 whose body says only 'Completion failed' — the real reason is in the log and in the halt audit event killSwitch.ts writes before throwing, not in the response. Also short-circuits ahead of the emit, so no SKU is emitted for the halted call.

_swallowNote: The three non-200 rows are the caller-visible statuses of the enclosing POST /api/ai-gateway/complete route, which is where these throws surface — this INTERNAL_FUNCTION has no HTTP surface and, by the try/catch above, no failure of its own that anything can observe synchronously. That asymmetry is the point of the file: the SKU-switch effect is verified in the audit payload (credential_source) and the persisted ai_gateway.completion.billed_cost, never in a response body.
